Image (0004.jpg) shows dents and scrapes on both the driver's door AND the rear door. The customer's story describes only a 'small dent' from a runaway supermarket trolley — a cause that would typically damage a single door panel. Two-door damage is inconsistent with a trolley impact, and the repair estimate (€3,225 covering driver door, rear door, and door sill trim) is disproportionate to the stated cause. Customer CUST-1013 had a prior parking-lot claim 10 months ago, and risk notes flag potential damage under-description. Image-claim consistency is below threshold; manual review required per Clause 5.1 / Clause E.6.

Image (0015.jpg) shows a significant dent on both the front quarter panel and the driver's door. The customer describes only a 'light graze' leaving 'a small mark near the front' — a description that materially understates the medium-severity two-panel damage visible in the image. The repair estimate (€2,570 covering front quarter panel, driver door, and door seal) is inconsistent with the story. Customer CUST-1014 is on a very short policy tenure (6 months since 2026-01-01). Evidence inconsistency triggers manual review per Clause 5.1 / Clause E.6.

Image (D0023.jpg) shows the rear windshield shattered with large holes — the appearance is inconsistent with hailstorm damage (which produces multiple small radial cracks) and inconsistent with the customer's description of 'windshield' damage (front). The image shows the rear window. AUTO-COMP-001 does cover hail under Clause 1.5, but the visual evidence does not support the claimed cause. Additionally, this is customer CUST-1015's third glass claim in 24 months (prior claims April and December 2025), triggering high claim frequency under Clause 5.4. Glass payout if approved: €1,380 × 100% = €1,380 (under €1,500 sub-limit).

Image (G0021.jpg) shows a rear windshield fully shattered with broken glass fragments around the frame. The customer's story describes a stone chip that 'spread into a crack' — a crack pattern is fundamentally different from a fully shattered window, suggesting the true cause may involve a heavier impact. Repair estimate (€1,550) exceeds the AUTO-COMP-001 glass sub-limit of €1,500, requiring manual approval. Customer CUST-1016 has two prior claims in 24 months (one late-reported), and this is their third claim — triggering Clause 5.4 high-frequency review. Payout capped at €1,500 glass sub-limit.

Image (S0022.jpg) shows burn damage on the rear bumper and taillight. The customer reports a rear-end collision with crushed panels — there is no collision damage visible, only burn damage. This is the textbook inconsistency example cited in auto_exclusions.md Clause E.6. Burn damage is explicitly excluded under AUTO-STD-001 Clause 2.1 (fire and burn damage requires a comprehensive policy). The repair estimate (€3,800, plausibility: suspicious) lists collision-repair parts that contradict the visible burn evidence. Customer CUST-1017 has a prior claim that was rejected after investigation found the damage was pre-existing. This profile and the strong image-story mismatch together indicate high fraud risk.

Image (F0022.jpg) shows only a shattered rear windshield with the rest of the vehicle appearing undamaged. The customer claims a head-on collision with deployed airbags, a completely crushed front end, and damage to both front quarter panels, hood, and bumper — none of which is visible in the image. The repair estimate (€6,500, plausibility: suspicious) lists front-end structural parts entirely absent from the photograph. The actual visible damage (glass only) would itself be excluded under AUTO-STD-001 Clause 2.4. Customer CUST-1018 shows an escalating payout pattern (€1,020 → €2,860 → now €6,500 claimed), a strong fraud signal documented in risk notes.

No damage photograph was submitted. AUTO-STD-001 Clause 1.2 requires a photograph for parking and single-vehicle claims; absence triggers mandatory manual review under Clause 5.2 and Clause E.8. The repair estimate (€1,980, plausibility: unclear — no image to verify) cannot be cross-referenced against visible damage. Adjuster will determine whether the claim can be settled on the customer statement and estimate alone. If approved: payout = 1980 × 0.80 − 500 = €1,084. Customer CUST-1019 has one prior claim and risk notes document this evidence gap.

Image (S0016.jpg) shows severe crumpling, shattered glass, and structural deformation across the driver's door, front quarter panel, windshield, and roof — consistent with the high-speed roundabout side-impact story. Three independent manual-review triggers apply: (1) the claim was reported 47 days after the incident (31–90 day window, valid hospital and police documentation provided, per Clause 4.2/5.5); (2) calculated payout = 14500 × 0.80 − 500 = €11,100, exceeding the €5,000 AUTO-STD-001 manual-approval threshold (Clause 5.3); (3) customer CUST-1020 has three prior claims in 18 months — hitting the ≥3-in-24-months frequency threshold (Clause 5.4) with escalating amounts and a prior late report. Despite the strong evidence match, all three triggers independently require adjuster sign-off.
